text:
Marta: Heads-up — BankNord (EU enterprise) wants a short POC but their security lead insists: all inference and prompt data must never leave EU. They asked if hosted can be configured to meet this and what extra costs look like.

Alex: Quick note: hosted inference data paths can be geo-locked to EU regions. Control-plane signals (metrics/telemetry) currently cross to us-east unless we deploy a Private control plane. Need to confirm whether BankNord will accept that distinction.

Sophie: Security POV: two main asks from them: 1) subprocessor attestations for every EU region used; 2) ability to bring their own KMS for key control. For hosted, BYO-KMS is limited — we support envelope encryption with partner HSMs in specific agreements, full BYO-KMS is standard for Dedicated/Private.

Marta: They explicitly asked for fail behavior: if EU capacity exhausted, either queue/hold or return 429 rather than routing to non-EU. Is that implementable?

Carlos: Yes — we have a residency enforcement mode that can return 429/reject. We can also queue briefly but that requires operational acceptance. Example policy snippet we can give them: 

```
residency_policy:
  tenant: banknord-2026
  data_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
  control_plane_region: us-east-1  # note: control plane signals may cross unless Private
  fail_behavior: reject  # options: reject | queue | fallback
  max_queue_seconds: 30
  subprocessors_allowed: [aws-eu-west-1, azure-northeurope, datadog-eu]  # example
```

Sophie: I'll produce the certified subprocessor list (ISO27001/SOC2 mappings) and a short blurb explaining the envelope-KMS limitation for hosted. Also will flag whether any monitoring vendor in the pipeline has non-EU egress.

eng-bot: Ticket SR-3019 created: "BankNord EU-geo POC: subproc attestation + residency policy". Assigned: eng-platform, security. ETA: 72h for initial bundle.

Nate: Pricing roughball: hosted geo-locking itself is not billed separately but SLA/reserved capacity is. If BankNord wants guaranteed capacity for the POC (3-day, 2 vGPU nodes equivalent), estimate: $3,500/mo (pro-rated) reserved POC fee. BYO-KMS envelope onboarding: $8k one-time, $400/mo key handling. Private control-plane + on-prem proxy requires custom SOW.

Marta: Can we offer a cheap Dedicated trial instead if they insist on full BYO-KMS and control-plane in EU? They'd prefer to avoid lengthy procurement.

Carlos: Short Dedicated pool for POC is doable; needs 2-3 business days to stand up once DPA is signed. Ops will need an explicit SOW stating fail_behavior=reject to avoid accidental cross-region routing.

Sophie: Legal note: the DPA needs to enumerate subprocessors and control-plane behavior. If BankNord will not sign unless control-plane resides in EU, we should offer Private or Dedicated with control-plane placement in EU as an add-on and flag lead time.

Marta: Action items: 
- Sophie: upload subprocessor/cert bundle to SR-3019 and author short hosted vs dedicated BYO-KMS explanation.
- Nate: produce a POC cost sheet (hosted geo-lock + Dedicated trial + BYO-KMS add-on).
- Carlos: draft the SRE runbook for residency.fail_behavior=reject and steps to validate no cross-region egress during test.
- Alex: confirm with product whether control-plane can be made EU-resident for Dedicated within standard options.

Nate: I'll have the draft cost sheet by EOD tomorrow.

Sophie: Uploading initial cert pack to SR-3019 in ~36h.

Carlos: I'll drop the runbook into the ticket and include test harness commands (curl + tcpdump) by tomorrow afternoon.

Marta: Cool. I'll set a call with BankNord security for Friday to walk through the policy and costs. tagging @eng-bot for updates. :calendar:
